title: Reuters, via Infobae: Binance loot reportedly laundered through THORChain and a bitcoin coinjoin service
date_note: Infobae gives only its own publication day, 27 November, for the Reuters-based report.
geo_basis: country: US authorities' attribution as relayed; no city stated
summary: Infobae, citing Reuters, says Chainalysis and Elliptic estimate that 'más de USD 600 millones' of the loot passed through THORChain, and that Elliptic reported 'USD 342 millones' went through a bitcoin coinjoin mechanism. Reuters puts the theft at 'USD 6.300 millones', and US authorities attribute the 29 October theft to North Korean hackers, Infobae says. Bitcoin.com News adds that on 31 October the FBI urged providers to block the funds, naming Thorchain.
plain: Infobae, relaying Reuters, reports that part of the money stolen from Binance on 29 October is being laundered through THORChain and a bitcoin mixing service. US authorities blame North Korean hackers.
exec: Infobae, citing Reuters, reports analysts tracing Binance loot through THORChain and a bitcoin coinjoin service.

evidence.quote: Los investigadores de Chainalysis y Elliptic estiman que más de USD 600 millones del botín pasaron por ella.
Elliptic informó que USD 342 millones pasaron por este mecanismo
Reuters lo cifra en USD 6.300 millones

validation.note: Infobae (citing Reuters) and Bitcoin.com News each state the more-than-600-million Thorchain estimate by Chainalysis and Elliptic and the Elliptic coinjoin figure. Reuters original not read; mdzol answered 403.

review.note: Compared 600M, 342M, 6.3B figures, 29 Oct, North Korea attribution, FBI 31 Oct against Infobae and Bitcoin.com News; two publishers state the estimates
